resources.string: Fewer ads and trackers in every app, without an account.
Guardian checks the names apps look up (DNS) on this phone and blocks known ad and tracker servers. It runs only on your phone: no account and no server of ours.
It is not a VPN to another country: it does not hide your IP address or encrypt your other traffic. Android shows a key icon because Guardian uses the system VPN interface to filter DNS locally.
Keep it on after a restart
In Settings → Start automatically, turn on Always-on VPN for Guardian. Android then starts it by itself.
Known ad and tracker servers are blocked in all apps.
Turn on to block ads and trackers in all apps.
Private DNS is on in system settings. Some lookups may go past Guardian.
Encrypted DNS cannot reach %1$s, so lookups fail. Choose another provider or turn it off.
Turn on protection to see what gets blocked.
Only DNS lookups go through Guardian. Allowed lookups go to your current network\'s DNS servers. Nothing is logged to storage.
Only DNS lookups go through Guardian. Allowed lookups go encrypted to %1$s. Nothing is logged to storage.
If an app or site stops working, tap Allow on its row.
Now allowed by the built-in list: %1$s

If you are worried about someone close to you: do not delete anything yet, save evidence (screenshots), and plan with someone you trust or a support organisation. If you fear a government or a professional attacker, treat this phone as exposed and use a different, clean device for sensitive things.
Guardian alerts you when an app contacts a known stalkerware server, while protection is on.
The stalkerware server list is unavailable; no alerts can be raised.
Each button opens a system settings screen. Guardian cannot see or change these settings itself.
Apps use the advertising ID to link your activity across apps. On Android 12 and later, deleting it gives apps a blank ID.
Apps with precise location can know where you are to within a few metres. Many work fine with approximate location.
Open an app to see its permissions. On Android 11 and later you can also turn on removing permissions if the app is not used.
An app contacted the servers of the stalkerware %1$s
This phone contacted the website or servers of the stalkerware %1$s
An app contacted the servers of the monitoring app %1$s
Guardian cannot tell which app it was.
If you were only reading about it in a browser, you can ignore this.
Apps like this also have legitimate uses (parental control, remote work). If you did not install it yourself, take a look.
Domain: %1$s. %2$s Not blocked, so whoever installed it is not tipped off. Open Guardian to see how to handle this safely.
Strict — most blocked; some sites or apps may break, use Allow to fix

Off: allowed lookups go to your network\'s DNS servers, unencrypted. On: they go encrypted (DNS over TLS) to the provider you choose, which then sees them instead of your network. If the provider cannot be reached, lookups fail; Guardian never falls back to unencrypted DNS.
Swiss non-profit; also blocks known malware domains
Encrypted DNS: %1$s, used while protection is on
Encrypted DNS: cannot reach %1$s. Lookups fail until it can be reached (no unencrypted fallback).
Rules: %1$d blocked, %2$d allowed by you, %3$d blocked by you
%1$d allowed by you, %2$d blocked by you
%1$d to block, %2$d to allow, %3$d lines skipped
Could not open the file picker
In system settings, tap the gear next to Guardian and turn on Always-on VPN. Android then restarts Guardian after a reboot.
Guardian follows your phone\'s language. You can choose another language for Guardian only in system settings.
Guardian follows your phone\'s language (English, Chinese, German, Japanese).
The German and Japanese texts are drafts written by AI and not yet reviewed by native speakers.

Guardian is free software (GPL-3.0-or-later) with no account, no analytics and no server of its own. The code is mostly written by AI to written specifications, then tested and reviewed before merging.
